findings.passage: “This is commonsense measure to ensure voters are who they claim to be,” Mastriano said. “Pennsylvania needs to take steps like this to regain the trust of voters, many of whom are currently very skeptical about the election process.
findings.note: Statement from his official Senate site on his vote for SB 1, which would send to voters a constitutional amendment requiring valid identification before casting a ballot.

findings.passage: Requiring voters to authenticate their identity at the polling place and to vote by mail is necessary to protect the integrity of elections and access to the voting process.
findings.note: Same release. Applies identity checks to both in-person and mail voting.

findings.passage: “We can have election integrity and increased voter turnout at the same time,” Mastriano said.
findings.note: Same release, responding to the argument that ID laws reduce turnout; he cites Georgia's 2020 turnout.

findings.passage: “In the aftermath of the chaotic 2020 election, I drafted, introduced, and co-primed several bills to restore integrity to our elections.
findings.note: News release on his site. It then lists SB 403 (repeal no-excuse mail voting), SB 573 (poll watchers), SB 735 (constitutional amendment to mandate voter identification for all forms of voting), SB 819/821 (election commission) and SB 884 (end no-excuse mail voting and require signature verification).

findings.passage: “I welcome the eventual end of “no-excuse” mail-in voting in Pennsylvania.
findings.note: Statement on a Commonwealth Court ruling on Act 77.

findings.passage: Automatic registration makes it more difficult to verify the accuracy of our voter rolls. It significantly increases the likelihood of fraud, duplicate registrations, and the registration of non-citizens, illegal aliens, and temporary residents.
findings.note: Statement on the state's automatic voter registration at driver's license renewal; raises non-citizen registration and voter-roll accuracy.

findings.passage: The irony is that Shapiro is opposed to voter ID but wants to register everyone to vote who gets a government issued ID (license).
findings.note: Same statement; links voter ID to the registration policy.
